standard_prerequisites: the Goedel numbering gn of sentences
definability of a set of numbers by a formula in the standard model
core_obligations: Prove Tarski's theorem: no formula D(x) in the language of arithmetic defines the set of Goedel numbers of true sentences
proof_roadmap: Suppose D(x) defines truth: N satisfies A iff N satisfies D(gn(A)) for every sentence A
By the fixed-point lemma there is a sentence A with Q proving A iff not D(gn(A)); hence N satisfies A iff N satisfies not D(gn(A))
Combining with the supposition, N satisfies A iff N does not satisfy D(gn(A)) while truth of A should be equivalent to D(gn(A)) -- contradiction
difficulty_reason: The diagonal argument is complete in the source and short, but it leans on the fixed-point lemma, which must be understood as given.
